evidence.claim: OperationalDGraph node membership derives only from an application's current active_dmap.placements; a node with zero current placements gets no entry.
A node absent from the current OperationalDGraph cannot currently receive an empty operational slice automatically; the lookup fails closed with a hard error.
A present node having zero desired_services is structurally legal under the current schema and validator.
The desired_state contract, on both server and agent sides, currently allows only 'running' or 'completed'.
The agent acts on desired state only by iterating context.desired_services; an empty list enters zero per-service branches.
Existing rollback (M8 / native-process equivalent) is per-service, explicitly requested, and gated by a Stage107A finite-lease boundary check immediately before mutation.
Container runtime identity evidence already exists via datum.* Docker labels written at creation and checked at convergence.
Native-process managed identity already persists strong, restart-surviving evidence keyed by a stable per-(project,node,service) key.
Server-side authorization records prove an authorization was issued, not that the corresponding host mutation succeeded; no outcome/report-back channel exists.

ServiceArtifact execution_generation/execution_projection_digest are live/mutable with a monotonic high-water mark, so current artifact identity must not be substituted for historical runtime identity.
No generic missing-context delete-all/sweep/prune path exists in the agent or server reconciliation code.
D-Engine node membership remains a pure projection of the current accepted PlacementAuthorityView; a future cleanup mechanism cannot implicitly change it.

Current DDeploy acceptance/proposal persistence retains accepted-proposal and acceptance history (keyed, not pruned in production code) sufficient to derive previous-vs-current placement relationships.
v1/v2 canonical reference parity (CanonicalContractReferenceV1 vs ContractRefV2) is field-identical but achieved via manual normalization, not a shared type.

Operational authorization persistence is keyed by (project_id, node_id) only; a newer durable authorization overwrites the prior one for that key, so no durable history of old authorization snapshots is retained.
The ServiceArtifact registry retains only the current artifact content plus a generation high-water counter, not complete historical artifact snapshots.
DDeploy v2 (DDeployStateV2) mirrors v1's proposals/acceptances/active structure, and a v1-to-v2 transition preserves old v1 acceptance records (only the active pointer is retargeted).
Container datum.* labels and the static DispatchContainerMapping config carry no project_id/application_id/service_id/dmap_ref identity.

No server code path binds a fresh artifact assignment to historical (as-originally-placed) identity; every join resolves against the current registry, and a single unmatched service fails the whole node's context.

M8 rollback already excludes image/target-identity verification from blocking removal and never checks physical container labels before docker rm -f; its safety rests on trusted container_name plus authorization/lease freshness, not per-instance identity proof.
